newsitem.title: UK: TENNIS-SECOND DAY SNIPPETS FROM WIMBLEDON.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SECOND DAY SNIPPETS FROM WIMBLEDON.

text.p: Second day snippets at Wimbledon on Tuesday:

Quote of the day - "Don't stand there like the Statue of Liberty, give me some balls." American Jeff Tarango to a ball-girl on court four. The charming Tarango, whose behaviour in 1995 led to a one-year ban from the championships, lost in four sets to France's Rodolphe Gilbert

Stat of the Day - 65. The number of singles victories eighth seed Boris Becker has now had at Wimbledon after accounting for Spain's Marcos Aurilio Gorriz. Becker, forced to retire from last year's championships in the third round after rupturing a tendon in his right wrist, has played every Wimbledon since 1984.

Meter madness - Taxi drivers ferrying spectators from Wimbledon station to the All England Club increased prices by 50 percent overnight on Tuesday. The reason: to stay in line with other drivers found to be charging more for a similar journey from the nearest underground station.

Defenceless champions - Steffi Graf becomes only the fourth woman singles champion in the Open era to have failed to return the following year to defend her Wimbledon title. Evonne Goolagong won in 1980 but did not return in 1981, Billie Jean King won in 1976 and did not play the next year and Ann Jones won in 1969 but failed to come again in 1970. Seven-times Wimbledon champion Graf is not defending her 1996 title because of knee surgery.
